newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA's Browner to host environmental ministers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA's Browner to host environmental ministers.

text.p: Environmental ministers from eight countries will meet next week for talks focusing on the particular threats to children posed by dangerous chemicals and toxics, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Carol Browner said on Thursday.
Browner will host the Summit of Eight May 5-6 in Miami, with officials from the Group of Seven (G7) nations as well as Russia and the European Union participating.
In a briefing, Browner said the ministers would discuss setting health and environmental standards to protect children as well as adults.
They also will discuss problems of unsafe drinking water, research on endocrine-disrupting chemicals, effects of second-hand tobacco smoke on children and lead poisoning in children, Browner said.
"This is the first time that our ministerial conference will actually focus on the issue of children's environmental health," Browner said.
"We have worked very hard to make children the center of the agenda because we believe that science shows us that children are more susceptible to the threats from toxics," she said.

Browner said she and her counterparts from Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and Russia, as well as a representative from the European Union, also will discuss health effects of climate change brought on by heat-trapping industrial emissions, and ways that countries could cooperate more effectively to fight environmental crimes.
